item.title: The Though Farmer
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a humanoid SCP whose main objective appears to be the collection of, what will be labeled for ease of understanding, thought energy. The exact nature of this energy is unknown, however it is known that SCP-XXXX is able to use this energy to influence or cause events. It is also understood that each human has roughly equal amounts of thought energy and that animals posses thought energy in lesser quantities, with more intelligent and larger animals possessing more than other species. SCP-XXXX typically gains this energy by gathering followers for cults or religions it leads or influences, however other methods have been recorded, with varying success.

+ show block
– hide block

The nature of the cults ran by SCP-XXXX is almost always non-violent, as SCP-XXXX seems to be be benevolent towards human and animal life and most recorded incidents of violence from an SCP-XXXX ran cult are directed towards insects and micro-organisms. SCP-XXXX begins its extraction process by introducing a religion or cult it is involved with to it's target, via use of its existing thought energy. SCP-XXXX will then manipulate it's target to focus on its cult by appealing to things the target enjoys, such as hobbies. It is at this stage that the target will either decide to become involved in the cult and proceed to the next stage, or will decide that they are uninterested, at which point SCP-XXXX will no longer interfere with their lives. If the target does decide to become involved, they will begin to become involved in the cult. Common activities at this stage include regular prayer times and regular meeting, both usually on a weekly basis. After taking part in these activities for about one to two and a half months, the target will enter the final stage. During this stage, the target will become more and more involved in cult activities until they take up a significant amount of the target's available time. The target will begin to sacrifice all 'optional' activities, including spending time with a significant other to make time for cult activities, however it will still take part in necessary daily activities, including eating meals, going to work and basic hygiene activities such as taking a bath or shower and brushing their teeth. During this stage the target will also have decreased cognitive functions, recording on average a 25% decrease in cognitive functions. There is currently no known way to exit this stage, barring termination of the subject, however research is ongoing. There are currently 2260 people under the effects of the

SCP-XXXX itself is a non-corporeal entity that is capable of appearing as almost any animal or person, including animals and people that do not currently exist. SCP-XXXX only appears to communicate with individuals it does not intend to use to gain additional thought energy. SCP-XXXX is capable of appearing in dreams of individuals it is trying to effect, as well as appearing in the 'real' world (For lack of a better word.). SCP-XXXX appears unable to manifest on electronic display devices though it can still appear to the viewer(s) of the device, but does not show up on any recordings of the encounter. There has also been no recorded physical interaction with SCP-XXXX to date, and it is incapable of moving objects, however while within and individuals dream it is capable of moving objects. SCP-XXXX has also been observed on several occasions interacting with foundation personnel. It appears to have no desire to harm foundation however due to the effects of SCP-XXXX it is advised that unnecessary communication with SCP-XXXX be kept to a minimum.
SCP-XXXX current motives are unknown, however there are some recorded conversations between foundation staff and SCP-XXXX that are on display in it's file.

Central Narrative: This SCP article focuses on SCP-XXXX's activities, what religions and cults SCP-XXXX has interfered with in history (that the foundation can find) SCP-XXXX's current endeavours, it's motives and communication with the foundation and, ultimately what it will do with its power (besides get more).

Hook: Theres a lot I could put here, but I envision the main hook as the process that SCP-XXXX 'gains' additional people, as well as its interactions with the foundation and its end goal with what it wants to accomplish (which will partly be a mystery, to maintain intrigue.).

Notes: While the whole emphasis on SCP-XXXX's motives and goals seems lacking in this greenlight/ idea critique post, I will include some conversations that foundation personnel have had with the SCP that will go more in depth on the subject. It is very hard to include that here.
And yes, I do know that this is a very long post for the idea critique forum, but I believe that I at least have to describe this SCP in some detail, as what I have included here is already quite sparse. Sorry if its a long read though. (IDK how to do the minimizing/clickable box thing very well.)


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. Also, please note the Ideas Critique required reading wordcount limit; your post is about 410 words over. Please address this before seeking further feedback. ~Zyn

item.title: Re: [Seeking Greenlight] Host of the Eldritch Abomination.
item.content:encoded:
So this feels like a few common tropes thrown together: monster/human hybrid (which was Lovecraft's allegory for mixed race relations, because he was a horrible racist), a reality bender, using an anomaly to "get rid of other anomalies", a spooky cult with ties to the SCP's origins… etc.

For those reasons, as it stands this isn't something I would greenlight.

Yes, things that have been done before could be made to work, but only with a unique twist.

I would suggest you read a lot more articles to see what sorts of things work on the site nowadays, as opposed to what worked on the site back in its origins.

item.title: Re: LLUN Man Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
you're going about it wrong. If you want to keep the article mysterious, that makes sense. It does not make sense to keep the idea post mysterious.

The purpose of the greenlighting process is to convince at least two authors that you can communicate your idea in a compelling manner.

So… I am not concerned that you would not explain the aura in the idea post, I am concerned that it seems to have no connection to the anomalies as presented. I feel like you missed the point of my critique.

I think you need to sit down and simplify, make a cohesive anomaly about the one man and focus on his anomalous aspects that thematically connect to each other.

When I said this ^ it was not to suggest anything but that your idea felt too disjointed and you should simplify the core anomaly to make more cohesive sense.

You need to develop a cohesive proposal for the idea to communicate what your story is about.

No one is going to greenlight your concept without you explaining the concept. If you choose to withold and say something like "you'll learn about it in the article" I wouldn't trust that this will turn into an article that could survive.

item.title: Tale: Rabbit Seed-bombs
item.content:encoded:
A deprecated house is over run by an anomalous, self-perpetuating, rabbit warren and their poo. Their previous owners still occupy the house.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: Tale

Genre (Optional): Dark Comedy

Elevator Pitch: Two Foundation agents are sent to investigate a house overrun by rabbits in the Midwest. The house is found to have its own microclimate similar to the Pacific Northwest, and its ecosystem is self-perpetuating due to the anomalous rabbits. The previous owners are turned into rabbit people by parasitic baby rabbits.

Central Narrative: It’s revealed through the found documents, an owner’s journals, that they had two rabbits. Before they could get them spade and neutered, the vets office closed due to quarantine. Unable to be contained, going so far as to teleport, the male rabbits kept escaping and creating more litters. The owners hired the city compost to take their quickly escalating piles of rabbit poo.

+ show block
– hide block

Over time, firs, ferns, blackberries, and other Pacific Northwest foliage grows out of the rabbit poo at an expedited rate. The owners, and housemates, slowly turn into rabbit-people when parasitic baby rabbits burrow into the base of their skulls. (Similar to the Goa’uld from Stargate).

Two Foundation agents are sent to investigate the house and they traverse room to room to figure out the ill fate of the owners. They are chased out of the house by angry rabbits, and rabbit-people.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A deprecated house is over run by an anomalous, self-perpetuating, rabbit warren and their poo. Their previous owners still occupy the house.

item.title: A teleporting bridge
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Other (Mystery/Curiosity)

Elevator Pitch: It's a teleporting bridge. It teleports whenever liquids or loose solids touch it, to a random waterway location. Containing it requires some experimentation and ingenuity, resulting in odd containment procedures that induce curiosity in readers who don't know what the anomaly is yet.

Central Narrative: The exacting, atypical containment procedures will lead the reader to wonder what anomaly is being contained. The description will answer that question, while prompting the reader to wonder why the containment procedures are so elaborate. The experiment log clarifies how researchers determined that simpler containment procedures were ineffective/insufficient.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The containment procedures involve the creation of an artificial miniature river ecosystem. Readers' expectations/hypotheses about the contained anomaly will be continually challenged or subverted by additional information in the containment procedure.

Additional Notes: This is my first SCP.

This revised post contains 143 words.

item.title: Re: (Awaiting greenlights) The elite soldier.
item.content:encoded:
Hey author, just pitching in my 2 cents.

This is really out of character for Anderson Robotics. Though this is not the first time they make an exoskeleton, it's certainly the first time they would be making a weapon of war! They're mostly known for making consumer grade products and fancy gizmos for the wealthy. A fighting exoskeleton that commits war crimes is definitely not something they would do. But that isn't to say Anderson Robotics isn't a moral bastion. Vincent Anderson, the founder, is known for being a cheat and a bit of a ruffian. There's also the fact that most AR products are powered by souls, which can lead to ethical questions.

Then there's the issue of the idea. Like zyn said, it's very typical of exoskeleton tropes and doesn't have much of interest going on for it.

item.title: Re: Television POV(Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for the critique. After several days of brainstorming I came up with the idea of a researcher obsessed with finding his own point of view. He'd try to use d-classes to flip the channels for him. Once that proves to be ineffective as they'd only be able to get a couple million in a year, he opts to find ways to dampen the signal, he'd find out that a lead-lined room works and it decreases the range considerably to around 40 kilometers. After that he discovers a d-class pov, he'd get the d-class to stare into the tv. The d-class does and enters into the trance. The researcher shuts off the tv and after five minutes the d-class comes to, but the d-class can't remember anything, much to the researcher's frustration. Several days later, the d-class kills himself.

This piques the researcher's interest even more. "what did he see that compelled him to commit suicide?" So, much to the dismay of the other researchers, he finds his own pov.

The ending is from another researcher who writes that the first researcher looked very unaware of his surroundings, suffered terrible disassociation and ultimately killed himself. Concludes that any researcher who wishes to test the SCP must do under supervision from another researcher.

item.title: Re: Unforgettable
item.content:encoded:
► my detailed thoughts◄
- close

The Addendum will have a journal where the main story takes place.

Be careful of doing a journal for the vast majority of the story… you can lose the reader this way, I’d suggest focusing on multiple types of addendums.

When his anomaly manifested, however, he began to draw away from his friends and family, out of fear that they would remember him in a bad way.

How is this anomaly discovered? As being memorable could easily never come to the attention of the Foundation.

That is, until his anomaly manifested. It's not known exactly when it happened, but he noticed how people began to act off around him. This "offness" became more intense over time, until people started to reference things he did that he had trouble remembering, leading him to realise that he was unable to be forgotten.

I’m sorry, I don’t know that such a leap is believable. People can remember things about yourself that you’ve forgotten very easily… it’s happened to me multiple times. I don’t think this fits as a realization moment. Need something a bit more dramatic to make the kid realize he can’t be forgotten.

He drew away from everyone he knew, drawing the attention of the Foundation as a consequence.

There are tremendous amounts of people who aren’t social and isolate, why would this draw the Foundation’s attention?

Overall:

  • I’m not super interested in this anomaly, as its so subtle I am not sure what would lead the Foundation would even discover it, let alone find it worrying enough to contain. For example, I don’t think knowing this person, and remembering a lot about them, would even necessarily be noticed or threaten normalcy… as I don’t know that people would realize it is something unnatural.
  • I am a little lost as to the core narrative here, what is the point of this story? Other than this kid becoming socially isolated due to his anomaly (which I am not entirely convinced would be a reaction to this specific anomaly) I am not seeing much in the way of an arc. I think you could make it interesting, but that would require a personal grounded description of this kid’s experiences. I think that’s something you should focus on if you’re going to continue with this.
  • ultimately I think you should consider tweaking the anomaly, making it a little less subtle… something that would make the person withdraw from the society, and even if you keep this anomaly, you’ve got to tweak the discovery as currently its not really explained how the Foundation would even notice it.

item.title: Re: LOOKING FOR GREENLIGHT/SCP Early concept: the greatest artist
item.content:encoded:
Responding to PM request (even though I'm listed as not taking requests for the time being, but hey, 'tis the season, right?)

So, I'm admittedly not super impressed here. I think there's a decent base to work with in regards to what the anomaly is capable of, which is shape-shifting into this very specific thing of art style mimicry. Giving it a personality centered around fascination of how humans express themselves through art is a good trait and can be tied into a narrative very neatly, I think.

There are, however, some snags that are keeping me from really enjoying this. There's this underlying murderous intent that doesn't make any sense to me. There's this drive to "be good at art" that feels contrived. And these are two big aspects of the character, making them kind of glaringly not appealing.

Which is what I want to focus on a bit. I think the character of the anomaly here needs a bit of shaping up and applied to a narrative that makes sense for it. If the anomaly's fascinations revolve around the history of human art, then what do its goals become? Are its efforts of artistic expression rooted in a desire to be human? Does it have a unique inner conflict that it can only express through mastery of an artistic medium that it has yet to find? People are often defined by their motivations and desires, which are often shaped by their past. What is this character trying to do, how does it get there, and what (if anything) gets in its way?

Feel free to reach out to me on IRC and we can talk this out a little more. I'm usually in all the chats, but it'd be better to hit me up in #thecritters.

item.title: Something, probably
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Maybe. I mean, yes, I mean…Idk man.

Page Type: Joke SCP, I think

Genre (Optional): Comedy, probably. Idk if Susan would like it.

+ Are you sure you want to open this?
- You're probably going to regret this.

Elevator Pitch: I think it's a 1979 Pontiac. Or an apple. Or a clock. Or Susan's cat. But it like, makes you doubt yourself when you talk about it. I think. Probably. I'm not sure. I'm not that good of a writer. I mean, some people say they like my writing, but Idk, you know? They could just be lying to make me feel better about myself. How am I supposed to know? Susan would know if she hadn't left me.

Central Narrative: A doctor probably tries to write the article about the object. But he keeps getting pulled into tirades about his poor life choices. I think. I mean, he might talk about why his wife left him. Or maybe he'll mention his slobbish lifestyle, and admit to eating three boxes of leftover pizza in the last week. Please come back, Susan. I love you.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It might be unique and original? Or not. Idk. It also may provide an interesting insight into the mind of a foundation researcher? Susan might like it. And it may be a bit funny? Or not. Idk. Also, it may be a bit relatable.

Additional Notes: A few closing notes:

  • I know the article falls into the "A thing that does a thing" trope, which is why I'm going to try and have the narrative in the article focus on the mind of the researcher creating the article, and hopefully highlight some common doubts we all have in a funny way.
  • In order to keep the article coherent, I may include the more story-ish portions in addendums at the end of the article.
  • Please Susan I really miss you

item.title: Kamen Rider but it's SCP
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Action

Elevator Pitch: If you're going to get a Magic Man to help make your superhero dreams come true, be sure you know what the hell you're doing. Otherwise you'll turn your friends into bugs and make demons out of your little sister's cancer.

+ Central Narrative
- Hide

A dumb teenager who's equal parts edgy and idealistic decides the world would be better if his favorite Japanese superhero were in it for realz. So he goes to his local Magic Man to ask for some magic, which he gets. He of course has no idea how to use it properly, so testing quickly starts going wrong. Using the magic superhero belt too long/too many times turns the wearer into a pile of bugs. Distraught after losing at least one friend, he reevaluates why he's doing this. The point of being a hero isn't doing cool moves or beating up bad guys, you see. It's about making a real change in the world. Cue a little bit more magic to try and help his little sister's cancer. Cancer turns into monsters/demons that can be fought in the real world, since you can't Rider Kick cancer without killing a little kid. Our protagonist vanishes after this, as does his sister.

This is later discovered by the Foundation after our would-be hero goes missing and cancer demons start terrorizing SoCal. The demons are the primary object, the belt is the secondary. Said demons can only be contained by someone using the belt (yes, this is a Thing What Makes You Fight Good skip, strike 1, I know), so you've got an MTF that's switching off different members being the 'hero' and fighting cancer demons while hoping desperately the next time they put it on, they don't turn into a pile of bugs. And that's about where the idea ends.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Man, if you're not already here to read SCP articles, I don't know how to hook you.

Additional Notes: Article will include hand-written journal entries with sketches, doodles and likely personally revealing notes.

item.title: Re: SCP: Older Brother (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi CringeSlayer. Let’s take a look at your concept.

+crit
-crit

Okay, so there’s potential here. You seem to be hinting at some wider conspiracy / mystery that has me intrigued to find out more. You also tease the entities’ origins and say it will be left open to interpretation. For the purposes of the greenlight, however, please expand on all these details below.

I also think you should be reconsidering the multiple anomalous properties. The young kid emits radiation, survives burns, and apparently can turn into a monster (like the Hulk). Then, the brother can emit white noise and has a psychic connection to the child? You see where I’m going with this? 1) How can nuclear testing result in so many anomalous properties? 2) Your concept is beginning to sound like the usual X-men mutants trope where multiple superhero powers are merely explained away “due to radiation”. It’s not very convincing. A much more plausible way to refine this would be to have the family all possess various degrees of the same powers, and not deviate the type of powers too much. Also, get rid of the psychic connection (unless you can decently explain why it happens). Seriously, it pushed the boundaries of realism for me.

But as the interviews go on, it becomes increasingly that the child keeping secrets.

Elaborate on this please. What secrets?

where these two came from and who "Mother" is

Similarly, please tell us in the conceptual stage.

Their origins might be linked to Russian nuclear testing

Are you going with this, or merely hinting at it? If it’s the latter, what is the actual origin of the family?

There's an important correlation between the Incredible Hulk comic and the pair that will be expanded on

Again, tell us what this correlation is.

If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll take another look. For now, all the best!

item.title: Re: Seeking greenlighting (or something idk i'm new here)
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi Ked Stand. Let’s take a look at your concept.

So I have a few issues with this concept, but at the same time, do take my comments with a grain of salt as I think it boils down to personal taste:

The object has too many anomalous properties, making it both overpowered, amalgamous and worst, unexplained. Is there a reason why you’ve assigned so many disparate powers to a single watch, such that it can reset time, pause time, give you a boost of energy and attach itself permanently to the user? It sounds as though you’ve simply tried to attach as many properties as possible to the object in order to make it sound cooler. Unfortunately, that’s not how we advise new writers to craft their scps.

Choose one (or two, max) anomalous properties and then try your best to explain how they function and why. You’ve got a discovery and test logs outlined already, but notice we don’t see any hint of who created this watch or what its designed purpose is.

tldr: pare down the anomaly to its main, most exciting qualities, then try to explain its backstory before proceeding. Again, this is just my opinion. Feel free to look for other reviewers if you want another. But if you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll take another look. For now, all the best!

item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi Galcedion. Let’s take a look at your concept.

So I like the fact you’re attempting to write a sci-fi scip, doubly so that it involves horror. My main problem with the concept is that it’s the basic plot of almost every Hollywood alien movie out there, mainly: crew goes on a mission, encounters alien they don’t understand, get murdered one-by-one etc. At this point, the genre is tried, tested, and cliqued, to be honest.

I know you’ve tried to give the alien more distinguishing characteristics, but still, the other dimension aspect is from Event Horizon, the melting of the crew into the walls is a page lifted from Aliens. What I’m saying is that the best way to distinguish a sci-fi scip from others is know what’s already out there and have a different origin story of your entity, if you’re sticking with the horror. Right now, you’ve said it’s “unknown”, and that just won’t cut it either. Encourage you to expand on this a little more.

item.title: Re: SCP instance naming
item.content:encoded:
so what exactly is this for?

Basically any sort of specific thing that is related to a primary anomaly, but distinct enough to make more sense to mention specifically. So if the Foundation was containing an anomalous field and there was an anomalous rabbit that only shows up in that field, the field would be SCP-XXXX and the rabbit would be SCP-XXXX-1. That helps prevent confusion/strange sentences where it would make sense to refer to only one thing at a time (for example, "SCP-XXXX-1 consumes solely dandelion greens" makes sense for the rabbit, not the field).

additionally I'm wondering if something like SCP-XXXX-1-1 would be acceptable or if it should just be referred to as SCP-XXXX-2.

It depends on what relationship that something has to SCP-XXXX-1. You would use an offshoot that has an existing designation offshoot number if you're referring to a specific part of that previously designated thing. To use the previous example, if the rabbit carried a good luck charm that had its own anomalous properties, that might be SCP-XXXX-1-1, though I think most authors would use SCP-XXXX-1-A or SCP-XXXX-1a or the like.

So basically:

  • SCP-XXXX: main anomaly/main collection of anomalies the Foundation is containing
  • SCP-XXXX-1: part of/a component of SCP-XXXX
  • SCP-XXXX-1-A: part of/a component of SCP-XXXX-1
  • and so on.

I don’t think it’s a balrog. If I were down in a burning coal mine fleeing for my life from a giant horned fire monster I wouldn’t stick around long enough to get a good look at it, especially since most of its body is probably obscured by smoke anyway. It’d be easy to confused among all the smoke and fire given off by the creature itself and the burning coal around it, so it’s no surprise that reports vary as to its appearance. A LotR fan is already going to expect a balrog when encountering a fire demon in an abandoned mine, so they’ll be more likely to mistake random shapes in the fire and smoke for wings and the iconic weapons. It’s just human pattern recognition at work.
